title: Sheaves of modules of finite type on the small etale site
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme, $Y_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] (final object $\mathrm{id}:Y\to Y$), $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $\Lambda_Y$ the constant sheaf of rings with value $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For an object $u:U\to Y$ of $Y_{\Et}$ write $\mathcal G|_U$ and $\Lambda_Y|_U$ for the restrictions to the localised site $Y_{\Et}/U$ (i.e. $V\mapsto\mathcal G(V)$ for $V\to U$ etale, viewed over $Y$), so that $\mathcal G|_U$ is a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y|_U$-modules. Say $\mathcal G|_U$ is *generated by finitely many global sections* if there are $n\ge0$ and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal G(U)$ such that the morphism $(\Lambda_Y|_U)^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$ of sheaves of $\Lambda_Y|_U$-modules sending the $j$-th basis section to $s_j$ is an epimorphism (Stacks 03DE (4), (5)). The sheaf $\mathcal G$ is *of finite type* if there is an etale covering $\{U_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ (a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms) such that each $\mathcal G|_{U_i}$ is generated by finitely many global sections. (Stacks 03DL (5) asks for every object $U$ of the site a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ with this property; for a site with a final object this is implied by the form above by base change of the covering, Stacks 03DF; only the form above is used.)

source.place: Definition 03DL (definition-site-local) (5), with Definition 03DE (definition-global) (4), (5) for 'generated by finitely many global sections'; Lemma 03DF (lemma-global-pullback) for the remark on the form over a final object
